claim: Rangen is the only Grand Cru on volcanic soil
because: The CIVA's own Grand Cru Kitterlé page (Guebwiller) describes a sandstone and volcanic terroir: at its western end the soil is volcanic-sedimentary Carboniferous grauwacke, the same kind of rock as Rangen's. The key (Rangen, the steepest and southernmost) still stands, but the word 'only' is false.
fix: Rangen is the best known of the Grands Crus on volcanic rock, and its slope is severe enough that growers carry washed-out soil back up the hill after storms. The wines are smoky and austere in youth.
